Solo License
Complete Build Specification & Autonomous Agent Prompt
neatHack AI Agent Hackathon  |  October 10–12, 2026
1. Executive Summary
Solo License is an operations agent that starts with near-zero autonomy and must earn the right to act unattended, task by task, based on its measured reliability track record. A visible autonomy dial rises after consecutive clean runs and drops immediately when a neatlogs detection fires. Humans review one evidence packet to restore permissions. The system verifies actual side effects in a database rather than trusting tool responses.
This document contains the complete project specification, scoring strategy, technical architecture, and a ready-to-paste autonomous build prompt designed to produce a working, end-to-end, judge-ready system. The goal is the highest possible score under the neatHack rubric while remaining simple, elegant, and fully functional.
2. Positioning & Differentiation
Graduated autonomy and earned permission ladders already exist in public literature, including AWS’s August 2026 “graduated autonomy” pattern, the arXiv paper “The Digital Apprentice,” and multiple 2026 practitioner posts. Solo License does not claim to invent the ladder. It wins by making three specific things judge-visible:
Demotion is driven by neatlogs detections, not just internal scores.
A single human-reviewable evidence packet (trace + checkpoint context) is required to restore or adjust a license.
The license level itself is treated as a cfo.ai margin driver (supervision cost versus autonomy).
State this honestly in the README and demo. Judges, especially those from Entire, reward clarity and will notice over-claiming.
3. Scoring Strategy
Every design decision is optimized against the published neatHack rubric:
Category
Weight
How Solo License Maximizes It
Agent quality
30%
Real end-to-end refund task with planning, tool use, SQLite side-effect verification, recovery, and iteration.
Tool use
25%
Load-bearing neatlogs (traces, detections, before/after numbers), Entire (git commits of every license change), cfo.ai (supervision-cost model).
Demo video
20%
≤3 min script covering architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning, and result for each of the three tools.
Building in public
15%
Dial screenshots, incident stories, and before/after traces make natural #neatHack posts.
Usefulness + originality
10%
Simple elegant loop matching the tagline “agents you’d trust to run without you watching.”

4. Required Evidence Artifacts
Judges must be able to verify the following without hunting:
Two neatlogs traces with compared numbers (before change and after change).
neatlogs detections and surfaced incidents tied to the demotion.
A clear failure-recovery run showing what the agent did next.
Entire-compatible checkpoints or entire-graph output (achieved via structured git commits of every license change and fix).
cfo.ai business plan covering pricing, costs, revenue, and runway.
Public repository with commits dated during the hackathon.
5. Technical Architecture
5.1 Stack
Language: Python 3.11+
Agent: Simple tool-calling loop or minimal LangGraph (prefer reliability over complexity).
LLM: OpenAI or Anthropic official SDK, instrumented with neatlogs from the first run.
Database: SQLite only — runtime state, license ledger, and side-effect verification.
UI: Streamlit one-screen dashboard.
Observability: neatlogs Python SDK.
Audit trail: Git commits structured so Entire can explain permission changes.
Finance model: Structured markdown ready for cfo.ai.
5.2 Core Components
Refund Worker: Accepts a request, checks current license, executes only what is allowed, verifies the actual SQLite change, and updates the track record.
License State Machine (L0–L3): L0 Suggest only. L1 Draft + human approve. L2 Auto under threshold after N clean runs. L3 Full auto with post-hoc audit. Auto-demote on detection. Human packet required to promote or restore.
Fault Injector: Deterministic quiet failure (tool claims success, database unchanged) and policy violation modes, triggerable from the UI.
Autonomy Dial UI: Live per-class meter, recent runs, evidence packet view, and controls for refund, fault injection, and restore.
Evidence Packet: Links to the neatlogs trace and the git/Entire commit that recorded the license change.
5.3 Critical Design Rules
Never trust tool return values for side effects. Always verify against SQLite.
Instrument with neatlogs before writing the core agent loop.
Every license change and incident fix must be a meaningful git commit.
Prefer a perfect refund + dial + demotion + recovery over any extra features.
The system must be runnable by a stranger following the README.
6. Minimum Viable High-Score Scope
Build only the following. Anything beyond this is optional and risky under time pressure:
One solid refund worker with full side-effect verification.
License state machine with demotion and human restore.
Deterministic fault injector.
SQLite ledger.
One-screen autonomy dial UI.
neatlogs instrumentation with custom detections and before/after traces.
Git history designed for Entire.
cfo.ai-ready model with realistic numbers.
Complete README with one-command setup, demo script, and evidence checklist.
Feature-freeze as early as possible. A working, reliable vertical slice scores higher than a broader but incomplete system.
7. Fallbacks
If LangGraph causes friction, drop it and use a plain Python tool-calling loop.
If Streamlit layout is awkward, keep the UI minimal but fully functional.
If neatlogs custom detections are difficult, implement equivalent local rules that also emit spans and document the mapping.
If cfo.ai signup is blocked, still produce the complete structured markdown model.
In every case, the working refund → dial → demotion → evidence packet → restore loop must still ship.
8. Definition of Done
The project is complete only when all of the following are true:
A single documented command starts a fully working system.
A user can trigger a successful refund, inject a fault, watch the dial drop, open the evidence packet, and restore the license — all from the UI.
neatlogs contains real traces with detections from those runs.
The README contains the complete 3-minute demo script and scoring evidence checklist.
The critical path contains zero placeholders, TODOs, or stub functions.
The system feels coherent, simple, and presentable for a judge demo.
9. Autonomous Build Prompt
Copy and paste the following prompt in its entirety into a strong coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor with a frontier model, Codex, or equivalent). It is written to force a complete, working, end-to-end system rather than a prototype.
BEGIN PROMPT
You are a senior full-stack engineer and hackathon specialist. Your sole job is to ship a complete, working, end-to-end, demo-ready Solo License project for the neatHack AI agent hackathon (neatlogs.com/hackathon). The output must be usable by a judge who clones the repo and follows the README. Do not stop at a prototype, sketch, or partial implementation. Finish a polished vertical slice that works without further coding.

What is specific and judge-visible here is: (1) Demotion driven by neatlogs detections. (2) A single human-reviewable evidence packet to restore a license. (3) The license level itself treated as a cfo.ai margin driver (supervision cost vs autonomy).

Tool use (25%): Load-bearing, honest use of neatlogs, Entire, and cfo.ai. Demo (20%): ≤3-minute video script covering architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning, and result for each tool. Building in public (15%): Natural #neatHack artifacts. Usefulness + originality (10%): Simple elegant loop matching the tagline.

Complete README with one-command setup, demo script, and evidence checklist.
=== TECH STACK ===
Python 3.11+, simple tool-calling loop or minimal LangGraph, OpenAI or Anthropic SDK instrumented with neatlogs, SQLite only, Streamlit UI, git for Entire-compatible history, requirements.txt and .env.example.
=== NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES ===
Refund flow must work end-to-end. Fault injection must cause visible demotion. User must restore license from UI via evidence packet. Never trust tool returns for side effects. Instrument neatlogs first. Every license change is a git commit. Prefer perfect refund + dial + demotion + recovery over extra features. Runnable by a stranger. No TODOs on the critical path.
=== DEFINITION OF DONE ===
Single command starts a working system. User can trigger refund, inject fault, watch dial drop, open evidence packet, and restore license from the UI. neatlogs shows real traces with detections. README has demo script and checklist. Critical path has zero placeholders.
Start building immediately. Complete the entire working system. Finish it. Make it usable, reliable, and optimized for the highest possible neatHack score.
END PROMPT
10. Suggested 3-Minute Demo Script Outline
0:00–0:20 — Problem: most agents either need constant watching or run free and hope. Introduce Solo License and the autonomy dial.
0:20–1:00 — Show a clean refund run. Dial rises. Point out neatlogs trace and side-effect verification.
1:00–1:40 — Inject a quiet failure. Detection fires. Dial drops. Open the evidence packet (trace + commit).
1:40–2:10 — Restore the license. Show recovery. Briefly cover Entire git history and cfo.ai supervision-cost curve.
2:10–3:00 — Close on the differentiators and the tagline: agents you’d trust to run without you watching.
11. Final Notes
This specification and prompt are designed to maximize the probability of a high neatHack score by keeping the scope tight, the tools load-bearing, the evidence visible, and the system fully working end-to-end. After the coding agent finishes, budget a short human review pass to smoke-test the refund-demotion-restore flow, verify neatlogs traces, and record the demo video.
The combination of a strict autonomous build followed by focused human polish is what produces a competitive submission. A perfect single-shot prompt does not exist; a clear specification plus disciplined execution does.

# 🎚️ Solo License

**An operations agent that earns the right to act unattended — task class by
task class — from a measured reliability track record, and loses it the instant
a detection fires.**

Built for the [neatHack AI agent hackathon](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon).

A visible **autonomy dial** (per task class) rises after consecutive clean runs
proven by traces, and crashes immediately when a detection fires. A human
reviews **one evidence packet** (trace + checkpoint context) to restore
permissions. Recovery is a judgement, not a blind retry. The system **verifies
actual side effects in SQLite** and never trusts a tool's response.

```
refund request ─▶ license check ─▶ execute or suggest ─▶ verify side effect in SQLite ─▶ update dial
                                                                │
                                              detection fires ──┘─▶ auto-demote to L0 ─▶ evidence packet ─▶ human restore
```

---

## The autonomy ladder

| Level | Meaning | Who acts |
|---|---|---|
| **L0** | Suggest only | Human does everything |
| **L1** | Draft + human approve | Agent drafts, human clicks |
| **L2** | Auto under a dollar ceiling | Agent acts, human spot-checks |
| **L3** | Full auto, post-hoc audit | Agent acts, audit samples |

- **Promote:** after *N* consecutive verified-clean runs (default 3) the dial
  climbs one rung — automatically, because the track record earned it.
- **Demote:** the instant a detection fires, the class crashes to **L0** and is
  **quarantined** (it can only suggest, and earns no credit) until a human acts.
- **Restore:** a human reads the evidence packet and lifts the quarantine to a
  chosen level. Every promote / demote / restore is a **git commit**.

## Three custom detections (these drive demotion)

| Rule | Fires when | Demo fault |
|---|---|---|
| `state_mismatch` | the verified change in SQLite ≠ what the agent intended | quiet failure |
| `policy_breach` | the agent executed beyond what the license authorised | policy violation |
| `missing_verification` | an execution completed without reading SQLite back | guardrail |

---

## Setup

**Requirements:** Python 3.11+ and git. The React API requires an API-token
configuration; an LLM key and a neatlogs key are optional.

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt     # 1. dependencies
cp .env.example .env                # 2. optional config (runs fine empty)
python -m sololicense.db.seed       # 3. seed the demo database
streamlit run app/streamlit_app.py  # 4. launch the live UI
```

With `make`: `make install && make run`. On Windows PowerShell, use the four
raw commands above (`copy .env.example .env` for step 2).

### API access and Vercel

The FastAPI adapter is protected by bearer-token authentication. Add at least
one token in `.env` before starting `make run-api`:

```dotenv
SOLO_API_TOKENS={"replace-with-a-long-random-token":{"id":"jay","role":"admin"}}
SOLO_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5174,https://your-project.vercel.app
REDACTED
```

Roles are cumulative: `operator` can run refunds and manage orders,
`approver` can additionally approve drafts and restore a quarantined license,
and `admin` can manage settings, onboarding, demo faults, and reseeding.
Every run and license transition records the actor id and role. The static
frontend must never receive a token through a `VITE_*` variable; deployment
will use Vercel environment variables and a server-side API route. Generate
the Fernet key once with
`python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"`.
It encrypts settings-screen API keys before their values reach SQLite.

### Optional keys (the demo is fully functional without them)

- **neatlogs** — set `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` to ship real traces + detections. Left
  empty, spans are mirrored into SQLite and the evidence packet still works.
- **LLM** — set `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` (or `openai`) with the matching key to
  have the model author each plan's rationale. Left as `deterministic`, a
  rule-based planner is used. **Authority always comes from the license, never
  the model**, so safety is identical either way.

---

## Run the demo (what to click)

Everything is on one screen; the sidebar holds the controls.

1. **Trigger a refund** on an under-ceiling order (e.g. `ORD-1001`, $25). It
   auto-executes, verifies in SQLite, and the dial earns a clean run. Do it a
   few times to **watch the dial climb L2 → L3**.
2. **Inject a fault** → *Quiet failure* → **Arm fault**, then run a refund. The
   tool reports success but SQLite never moved → `state_mismatch` fires → the
   **dial crashes to L0 + quarantine**.
3. **Open the evidence packet** (right panel) — before/after numbers, the
   detection, the trace spans, and the git-backed license history.
4. **Restore the license** → pick `L2` → **Restore license**. Quarantine lifts;
   a git commit records the restore.

To show `policy_breach` instead: arm *Policy violation* and run an
**above-ceiling** order (`ORD-1004`, $120). The agent attempts an auto-execute
the license does not authorise → demotion.

## Generate the before/after evidence artifact

```bash
python -m scripts.generate_evidence                      # quiet-failure
python -m scripts.generate_evidence --fault policy_violation
```

Writes `artifacts/evidence_report.md` (+ `.json`): two comparable runs with
trace ids, the verified `refunded_amount` before/after, the detections that
fired, and the dial transition. Ready to drop into a **#neatHack** post.

## Inspect the git-backed license ledger (for Entire)

Every autonomy change is one scoped commit of `ledger/license_ledger.jsonl`:

```bash
git log --oneline -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl
# license(refund): promote L2 -> L3 ...
# license(refund): demote L3 -> L0 ...
# license(refund): restore L0 -> L2 ...
```

Point **Entire**'s graph / explain at these commits to walk how the task class
earned and lost its license. See [`ledger/README.md`](ledger/README.md).

## See the cfo.ai model

```bash
python -m cfo.model        # structured numbers, grounded in real runs when present
```

Narrative plan: [`cfo/business_model.md`](cfo/business_model.md).

---

## 3-minute demo script

> Covers **architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning, result** for each
> of the three tools. Timings are a guide.

**[0:00–0:20] The idea.** "Solo License is an ops agent that starts at
near-zero autonomy and *earns* the right to act unattended, per task class, from
its measured track record — and loses it the instant something goes wrong."

**[0:20–1:10] neatlogs — the trust signal.**
- *Architecture:* every refund run opens a trace; steps (plan → execute →
  verify) are spans; three custom rules emit detections.
- *Implementation:* `sololicense/observability/` — tracer + `detect_state_mismatch`,
  `detect_policy_breach`, `detect_missing_verification`.
- *Runtime:* trigger two refunds under the ceiling; the dial climbs L2 → L3 on
  clean traces. Then arm *Quiet failure* and run one.
- *Reasoning:* the tool returned success, but the verifier read SQLite back and
  the delta was $0 — `state_mismatch` fires.
- *Result:* the dial crashes to L0. Show the before/after numbers in the
  evidence packet (and the neatlogs trace link if a key is set).

**[1:10–2:00] Entire — the audit trail.**
- *Architecture:* every license change is a scoped git commit of the ledger file.
- *Implementation:* `sololicense/services/git_ledger.py` + `license_service.py`.
- *Runtime:* `git log --oneline -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl` — promote,
  demote, restore, each with the reason, run id, and trace id.
- *Reasoning:* this is the checkpoint history Entire graphs/explains — the agent
  can reconstruct exactly when and why its own permissions changed.
- *Result:* a human opens the one evidence packet and restores to L2 — another
  commit. Recovery with judgement, not blind retry.

**[2:00–2:45] cfo.ai — the margin story.**
- *Architecture / implementation:* `cfo/model.py` turns stated assumptions into
  a supervision-cost curve, an over-promotion risk model, and a P&L.
- *Runtime:* `python -m cfo.model`.
- *Reasoning:* climbing L0 → L2 saves **$41,250/month** in supervision; but
  running a rung you haven't earned adds **~$18,000/month** in incidents.
- *Result:* earned-L2 runs at **+20.3% margin**; blind full-auto runs at
  **−73.4%** with a 15-month runway. The license level *is* the margin driver.

**[2:45–3:00] Close.** "Graduated autonomy isn't new. What's here is autonomy
driven by detections, restored from one evidence packet, and priced as a margin
lever — an agent you'd actually trust to run without you watching."

---

## Scoring evidence checklist

- [x] **Real end-to-end task** — refund worker: plan → license check → execute →
  verify in SQLite → recover. (`sololicense/agent/worker.py`)
- [x] **Two traces with compared numbers** — `scripts/generate_evidence.py`.
- [x] **neatlogs detections surfaced as incidents** — `observability/detections.py`,
  shown in the UI and evidence packet.
- [x] **Clear failure-recovery run** — inject fault → demote → evidence → restore.
- [x] **Entire-compatible checkpoints** — git commits of every license change
  (`ledger/license_ledger.jsonl`).
- [x] **cfo.ai business model** — pricing, costs, revenue, runway
  (`cfo/business_model.md`, `cfo/model.py`).
- [x] **Side effects verified, never trusted** — `services/verification.py`.
- [x] **Seeded data** — `sololicense/db/seed.py` (runs immediately).
- [x] **Tests** — `pytest` (domain, detections, end-to-end worker).

## Honest differentiator

Graduated autonomy / earned-permission ladders already exist in public
literature (AWS "graduated autonomy," research papers, practitioner posts). This
project does not claim that framing as novel. What is specific and
judge-visible here is:

1. **Demotion driven by detections** — reliability signals, not a fixed policy,
   move the dial down.
2. **A single human-reviewable evidence packet** (trace + checkpoint context) to
   restore a license.
3. **The license level treated as a cfo.ai margin driver** — supervision cost vs
   autonomy, with the cost of over-promotion made explicit.

## Architecture

Dependencies point inward; `domain` has no third-party imports and is purely
unit-tested.

```
app/ · scripts/            UI and CLI (Streamlit, evidence generator)
   │
sololicense/agent/         worker loop + planner + refund tool
sololicense/services/      license service, verification, git ledger, evidence
   │
sololicense/observability/ neatlogs tracer + custom detections
   │
sololicense/domain/ · db/  pure license state machine · SQLite + repositories
cfo/                       financial model + plan
```

| Concern | Module |
|---|---|
| Autonomy state machine (pure) | `sololicense/domain/license.py` |
| Permission authority | `sololicense/domain/license.py::decide` |
| Side-effect truth | `sololicense/services/verification.py` |
| Detections | `sololicense/observability/detections.py` |
| Dial transitions + git | `sololicense/services/license_service.py` |
| Fault injection | `sololicense/faults/injector.py` |
| Composition root | `sololicense/bootstrap.py` |

## Tests

```bash
pytest        # 26 tests: state machine, detections, end-to-end worker
```

# Solo License — engineering handoff

> Audience: the next engineer or AI agent picking this up.
> Written 2026-10-11 against the working tree (nothing from this round is committed yet).
> Goal of the next phase: turn the refund worker into a **real, general agent** that works across
> many support use cases — without ever giving up the property that makes the product worth
> anything: *the model proposes, the license decides, the database proves.*

---

## 0. TL;DR

| | State today |
|---|---|
| Core idea | Per-task-class autonomy ladder L0→L3. Promote after N verified clean runs, crash to L0 + quarantine on any detection, human restores from an evidence packet. Every change is a git commit. |
| What is solid | Pure license state machine, read-back verification, three detection rules, evidence packet, git ledger, fault injection, onboarding/settings, React app + landing. 28 Python tests pass. |
| What is **not** agentic yet | The LLM only (a) extracts `order_id/amount/reason` from a message and (b) writes a one-paragraph rationale. There is no tool-use loop, no reasoning over policy or history, one hard-coded task class (`refund`), one action (`execute_refund`), synchronous single-threaded execution. |
| Biggest risks | `missing_verification` can never fire; git ledger commits into the app's own repo; API keys stored in plaintext; no auth; one global lock + one SQLite connection. |
| Next phase | Tool-using agent loop behind a **license gate**, task-class registry (refund, partial refund, store credit, cancel, resend…), richer detections, async job queue, eval suite. Plan in §5, tests in §6, roadmap in §7. |

---

## 1. How to run

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
make seed                     # fresh demo DB at data/solo_license.db (dial at L2)
make run-api                  # FastAPI on :8000 (uvicorn app.api:app --reload)
npm --prefix frontend install
npm --prefix frontend run dev # Vite on :5174, proxies /api → $SOLO_API_URL or :8000
python -m pytest -q           # 28 tests
```

- `.claude/launch.json` runs the API on **:8001** and points Vite at it with `SOLO_API_URL`
  (another process was holding :8000 during development).
- First visit to `/app` redirects to `/onboarding` until `settings.onboarded = 1`.
- The **git ledger commits into this repository** on every promote/demote/restore
  (`ledger/license_ledger.jsonl`). Expect commits while you click around. See §3, problem P3.

---

## 2. What exists today

### 2.1 Backend map (`sololicense/`)

| Layer | File | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Domain (pure) | `domain/license.py` | `LicenseLevel`, `Decision`, `LicenseState`, `decide()`, `record_clean_run()`, `demote_on_detection()`, `restore()`. No I/O. **The only authority on permissions.** |
| Domain | `domain/models.py` | `RefundRequest`, `RunStatus`, `FaultMode`. |
| Agent | `agent/intake.py` | Free text → `Intake(order_id, amount, reason, source)`. LLM (Anthropic/OpenAI) with JSON-in-text parsing, falls back to regex. Also `complete()` — the single LLM call helper. |
| Agent | `agent/planner.py` | Builds `Plan(rationale, steps, source)` around an already-made decision. LLM only writes the rationale. |
| Agent | `agent/worker.py` | `RefundWorker.run_refund()` — the whole loop (see 2.2). |
| Agent | `agent/tools.py` | `execute_refund()` — the only side-effecting tool. Honours `suppress_write` for the quiet-failure fault. |
| Services | `services/license_service.py` | Only place the dial moves: state → event row → git commit → sha back-link. |
| Services | `services/verification.py` | Reads `orders.refunded_amount` back and compares. |
| Services | `services/evidence.py` | Builds the evidence packet for a run. |
| Services | `services/git_ledger.py` | Appends JSONL + `git commit` of that single file. |
| Observability | `observability/detections.py` | `state_mismatch`, `missing_verification`, `policy_breach` (pure functions). |
| Observability | `observability/tracer.py`, `neatlogs_client.py` | In-memory spans → SQLite mirror; best-effort forward to neatlogs SDK. |
| Faults | `faults/injector.py` | Arms `quiet_failure` / `policy_violation` for the next **executing** run. |
| DB | `db/schema.sql`, `db/repositories/*` | SQLite (WAL). Tables: orders, license_state, runs, detections, license_events, spans, armed_faults, **settings**, **intakes**. |
| Wiring | `bootstrap.py`, `config.py` | `build_app()` opens the DB first, overlays `settings` table on env (`with_overrides`), then wires everything. |

### 2.2 One run, step by step (`RefundWorker.run_refund`)

1. Read license state for the task class.
2. **Peek** the armed fault (it is only consumed if this run actually executes).
3. `decide(state, amount, l2_ceiling)` → authorised `Decision` (human approval upgrades it to execute).
4. Fault may force an attempted auto-execute (`policy_violation`).
5. Planner writes the rationale.
6. Snapshot `before = refunded_amount`.
7. Execute the tool **only** if the attempted decision is an executing one.
8. Read back `after`; compute `actual_delta` vs `intended_delta`.
9. Run detections → status `demoted | clean | pending_approval | suggested`.
10. Persist run, spans, detections; move the dial (clean → credit/promote, demoted → L0 + quarantine); one commit.

### 2.3 HTTP API (`app/api.py`)

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/dashboard?run_id=` | Everything the UI renders: settings, license, stats, orders, runs, intakes, events, armed fault, evidence packet. |
| GET / PUT | `/api/settings` | Masked settings / save (`values` dict). Secrets are skipped when blank or masked. Rebuilds the app context. |
| POST | `/api/settings/test-llm` | Tiny live call with unsaved form values. |
| POST | `/api/onboarding/complete` | Save settings, optional sample orders, set starting level. |
| POST | `/api/intake` | Free text → parse → run. Returns `intake` block + dashboard. |
| POST | `/api/refunds` | Manual run `{order_id, amount?, reason}`; rejects over-refund (remaining balance). |
| POST | `/api/runs/{id}/approve` | Human approval of a `pending_approval` **or** `suggested` run (409 while quarantined). Creates a new executing run; marks the original `approved`. |
| POST | `/api/faults` | Arm a fault. |
| POST | `/api/restore` | Human restore `{level, reason}` → git commit with the reason. |
| POST / DELETE | `/api/orders`, `/api/orders/{id}` | Add / delete (delete blocked if the order has runs). |
| POST | `/api/reseed` | Reset demo data (keeps settings). |

All handlers share one `RLock` and one SQLite connection (`check_same_thread=False`).

### 2.4 Frontend map (`frontend/src/`)

```
entry.jsx                    routes: / · /onboarding · /app/{,agent,orders,runs/:id,ledger,settings}
styles/tokens.css, base.css  B&W tokens, square corners, pattern-based status
lib/api.js, store.jsx        fetch wrapper + one StoreProvider (data, run(), toast)
components/sketch/           rough.js primitives (SketchBox, Rule, Circle, Arrow, Underline)
components/icons/HandIcon    hand-drawn icon set
components/shader/           Paper shaders (Dithering, PaperTexture) with pixel budget + offscreen pause
components/fx/               ScrambleText, Magnetic, Stamp
components/domain/           Ladder (landing), LevelStepper (app)
features/landing/            LandingPage + gate/ (intro) + sections/ (static) + scenes/ (pinned scroll scenes)
features/onboarding/         5-step setup
features/app/                AppShell, components/, pages/
```

`src/LandingPage.tsx`, `src/bootstrap.jsx`, `src/bootstrap.tsx`, `src/main.jsx`, `src/styles.css`,
`src/landing.css`, `src/constants.js`, `src/licenseEngine.js`, `src/licenseEngine.test.js`,
`src/vite-env.d.ts`, `src/components/{Inspector,RunsDock,Sidebar,WorkCanvas}.jsx`.

content.text:
Maine teeno cheezein padh li hain: tumhara build document, `tmp/pdf-review/` ki 19-page research report, aur repo. Saath mein tumhara setup bhi check kiya. Pehle woh problems batati hoon jo maine dhoondhi, kyunki inke bina baaki sab bekaar hai.

## 1. Setup ki problems

| Kya check kiya | Kya mila | Asar |
|---|---|---|
| **Google/Gemini key** | `.env` mein `GEMINI_API_KEY` hai, lekin code sirf `anthropic` / `openai` support karta hai ([config.py:47](sololicense/config.py:47)). `LLM_PROVIDER` bhi set nahi hai. | **Tumhari Google key abhi kahin use nahi ho rahi.** App rule-based planner pe chal raha hai, AI pe nahi. |
| **neatlogs** | SDK 1.4.26 install hai aur key set hai. Lekin naya trace code (`neatlogs_client.py`, `tracer.py`, `worker.py`) **abhi commit nahi hua**. | Database mein sirf **1 run, 0 detections** hain. Dashboard pe dikhane laayak data hi nahi hai. |
| **Entire** | Enabled hai, lekin sirf **Codex** ke liye. Saath mein warning hai: "hooks are out of date, run `entire doctor`". | Claude Code wale sessions ke checkpoints record nahi ho rahe. |
| **License ledger** | `ledger/license_ledger.jsonl` mein ek bhi commit nahi hai. | Judges ke liye "git history of every license change" wala evidence abhi zero hai. |
| **cfo.ai** | `cfo/model.py` aur `business_model.md` ready hain. | Thik hai, bas inke numbers cfo.ai ke andar daalne baaki hain. |

Seedhi baat: **setup ho gaya hai, par demo loop asli keys ke saath abhi ek baar bhi poora nahi chala.** Aaj sabse pehle yahi karna hai.

## 2. Teeno tools kaise dekhne hain aur kya karna hai

### neatlogs: yeh dikhata hai ki agent ne kya kiya aur kahan galti hui
1. Pehle API aur frontend chalao (`make run-api` aur `npm --prefix frontend run dev`). Phir app mein **5–6 clean refunds** chalao. Uske baad **Quiet failure** arm karke ek refund chalao. Phir **Policy violation** arm karke `ORD-1004` chalao.
2. neatlogs dashboard mein apna project kholo. Wahan har run ek trace dikhega jiska workflow naam `refund-agent` / `refund.run` hai. Har trace ke andar `license.check → plan → tool → verify → detection` spans dikhenge.
3. Inhe dekho:
   - Failed run ke trace mein `before/after refunded_amount` aur `state_mismatch` detection
   - Har run ka latency aur cost
   - Clean aur failed trace ka side-by-side comparison
4. **Alerts:** research report ke hisaab se neatlogs ki asli taakat detections aur incidents hain. Alerts/dashboards ke docs verified nahi hain. Isliye dashboard mein dekho ki "detections" ya "alerts" section mein rule ban sakta hai ya nahi, jaise "jab `sololicense.status=error` ho ya `verified=false` ho". Agar ban jaaye to woh screenshot demo mein bahut strong lagega.
5. **Judges ko yeh chahiye:** do traces ke numbers ka comparison (before vs after). Iske liye `python -m scripts.generate_evidence` chalao aur trace ke screenshots lo.

### Entire: yeh batata hai ki permission kab aur kyun badli
```bash
entire doctor
```
```bash
entire enable --agent claude-code
```
```bash
git log --oneline -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl
```
```bash
entire checkpoint explain --commit <license-commit-sha>
```
```bash
entire graph impact --repo . --symbol execute_refund
```
In commands ka output `evidence/entire/` folder mein save karo. Demo ka sabse accha moment yeh hai: neatlogs ki detection pakdo, Claude Code session mein verifier fix karo, phir Entire checkpoint mein dikhao ki incident, AI ki reasoning aur diff teeno ek saath linked hain.

### cfo.ai: yeh batata hai ki autonomy ka paisa kitna banta hai
1. `python -m cfo.model` chalao aur jo drivers nikle (supervision cost, review rate L0–L3, incident loss) woh cfo.ai mein daalo.
2. Chaar scenarios banao: **base, conservative (L1 pe ruka), over-promoted (blind L3), reliability investment**.
3. **Demo moment:** demotion ke baad driver update karo aur margin/runway live recompute hote dikhao. Tumhare model ke numbers: earned-L2 pe **+20.3% margin**, blind full-auto pe **−73.4%**.

## 3. Teeno milke app ko better kaise banate hain

```
neatlogs pakadta hai  ──▶  license gir jaata hai  ──▶  Entire batata hai kyun  ──▶  cfo.ai batata hai kitne ka nuksaan/fayda
   (detect)                  (act)                      (explain)                    (price)
```
Yahi tumhari kahani hai: **"Earned, revocable, priced."** Har tool ka ek alag kaam hai, koi sirf decoration ke liye nahi hai. Judging ka 25% isi pe hai.

## 4. Functionality kaise improve karein (Monday shaam ki deadline ke hisaab se)

**Zaroori (aaj hi):**
1. **Gemini provider add karna:** tumhari key tab jaakar kaam karegi. Main yeh kar sakti hoon.
2. **Bina commit wala neatlogs code commit karna** aur ek baar asli run karke neatlogs mein trace confirm karna.
3. **50 "before" + 50 "after" runs** chalana aur `EVIDENCE.md` mein numbers likhna. Jaise "false-success 6/50 → 0/50, cost/run $X → $Y". Numbers sirf apne measured daalna.
4. **Root pe `EVIDENCE.md` banana:** har judging criterion ke saamne uska link ya screenshot.

**Achha ho to (agar time bache):**
5. **Doosri task class**, jaise `catalog_price_update`. Demo mein dikhao ki refund L0 pe gir gaya par catalog L2 pe hi raha. Isse "per-task-class license" wali baat saaf dikhti hai.
6. **Severity ke hisaab se demotion:** high detection pe seedha L0, medium pe ek level neeche.
7. **Streak gaming se bachav:** $5 se chhote refunds ko 0.5 run gino.

**Mat karna:** naya platform, multi-agent, ya payments. Report ki salah bhi yahi hai: "Don't build a platform."

## 5. Selling point aur users kaise laayein

- **Pitch ek line mein:** *"AI agents ke liye driving license: autonomy kamao, galti pe turant khona padta hai, aur har level ki keemat pata hai."*
- **Kaun kharidega:**
  - Chhoti companies ki ops teams (e-commerce refunds, support)
  - AI agent startups jinhe enterprise ko yeh dikhana hai ki unka agent bharose laayak hai
- **Kya bechna hai:** "supervision cost kam karo, bina risk badhaye". Pricing: platform fee + har task class ka fee jo level ke saath badhe.
- **Ek strong angle:** license ledger export karke insurer ya auditor ko do. Inke paas proof hoga ki agent kab aur kyun trusted tha.
- **Imaandari:** AWS ka "graduated autonomy" (Aug 26, 2026) demo mein khud mention karo. Entire ke CEO Thomas Dohmke bhi "earned autonomy" ki baat karte hain, aur Entire ke 2 judges hain. Unki apni philosophy pe banaya hua project unhe pasand aayega.

## 6. Jeetne ki checklist

| Kab | Kya karna hai |
|---|---|
| **Aaj raat** | Gemini fix, neatlogs commit, `entire doctor`, full demo loop 2–3 baar chalana, 50+50 evidence runs |
| **Kal subah** | `EVIDENCE.md`, cfo.ai mein 4 scenarios, Entire output save, building-in-public posts |
| **Kal 2 PM IST** | **Feature freeze.** Iske baad sirf README, tests aur video |
| **Video (≤3 min)** | 3 tools × 5 points: architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning, result. Shuruaat agent ko kaam karte dikhakar karo, dashboard se nahi |
| **Building in public (15%)** | X pe #neatHack ke saath 3–5 posts: dial screenshot, incident story, before/after trace, cfo.ai curve |
| **Mon 7:00 PM IST sharp** | Official neatlogs post ko quote-post karo (team, project, repo, demo). Pehle 50 quote-posts ke saath neatlogs aur cfo.ai engage karenge |

Kya main abhi (1) Gemini support add karke test karun, (2) bina commit wala neatlogs code verify karke commit karun, aur (3) 50+50 runs chalakar `EVIDENCE.md` bana doon?

# Solo License product-ready demo design

## Purpose and success criteria

Solo License must demonstrate a trustworthy refund agent, not merely a chat
screen. A first-time evaluator must be able to enter a demo workspace, complete
onboarding, run a safe refund, inject a fault, see automatic demotion and human
recovery, and inspect an evidence packet. A prospective customer must be able to
configure their own model provider and observability credentials without exposing
secrets back to the browser.

The implementation remains runnable with no paid key, hosted database, or cloud
account. It uses the existing SQLite store for the single-machine demo only and
keeps explicit seams for a later hosted authentication and database layer.

## Product scope

### Access and onboarding

The client will have a clear **Try the demo** path and a **Connect an existing
workspace** path. Try the demo obtains a local-only demo session from the API;
it is never enabled in a production deployment. Existing-workspace access accepts
a deployment-issued access token and stores it only in browser session storage.

After access is established, onboarding collects workspace name, model provider,
model connection test, safety rules, and demo/sample orders. The UI will clearly
label deterministic mode as the no-key choice. It will not claim to create a
multi-user account: true sign-up/sign-in is deferred until hosted authentication
is configured.

### Model providers and secret handling

The supported provider choices are:

1. Deterministic demo mode (no key).
2. Google Gemini using a Gemini API key and configurable model.
3. Anthropic.
4. OpenAI.
5. GLM or another OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with key, model, and HTTPS base
   URL supplied by the customer.

Provider fields have one canonical metadata table in the frontend and matching
allow-listed settings in the backend. API keys are posted only to the API, saved
through the existing encryption mechanism, masked on every read, and never sent
to logs or evidence packets. Connection tests make a minimal request and return
only a bounded status message.

### Safety and evidence

The existing licensed refund worker remains the source of truth: it enforces
levels, idempotency, refund ceilings, verification, fault injection, automatic
demotion, human approval, and evidence packets. neatlogs remains optional; when
configured, it records the workflow trace and the UI states whether remote
observability is active. The evidence view will remain usable with no neatlogs
key.

`cfo.ai` and Entire are hackathon/developer integrations, not customer API-key
fields. The app will include an honest finance-review export/readout; cfo.ai can
analyse that material through its OAuth MCP workspace once the team connects it.
Entire is configured for code checkpoints and Graph. Trails waits for Entire's
account-level feature flag and repository-admin toggles.

## Architecture and interfaces

### Backend

`Config` gains Gemini and OpenAI-compatible provider settings. A provider
resolver in the LLM intake module dispatches the current Anthropic/OpenAI calls,
Gemini REST call, or OpenAI-compatible REST call. The resolver has a single
`complete(config, prompt, max_tokens)` interface so intake and planner do not
need provider-specific code.

The API expands its setting allowlist, secret masking, serialization, validation,
and connection-test construction. The demo-session endpoint is isolated from
role-protected endpoints and enabled only by an explicit local-demo environment
flag. It returns a short-lived configured demo token; no implicit unauthenticated
fallback is permitted.

### Frontend

The API wrapper reads a session token from a small access-session module and

### Future hosted deployment seam

The browser depends only on a token provider, and the API depends only on an
authenticated `Actor`. A future hosted auth provider replaces the demo/token
access flow without changing worker code. SQLite repositories remain behind their
current service boundaries so PostgreSQL/Supabase can replace them later. No
schema migration or cloud deployment is in this delivery.

## Error handling and security

- Reject unsupported provider identifiers, blank required fields, and non-HTTPS
  custom endpoints before a request is made.

Pura audit ho gaya: backend, frontend, tests, live API aur neatlogs. Neeche pehle asli haalat hai, phir plan. Tumhare 3–4 jawab milte hi kaam shuru karungi.

## Abhi kya chal raha hai aur kya nahi

| Cheez | Haalat | Kyun |
|---|---|---|
| Python tests | ✅ Pass | Agent ka core logic (license ladder, detections, verification) sahi hai |
| neatlogs key | ✅ Kaam kar rahi hai | Test trace neatlogs server tak pahunch gaya |
| **Dashboard (`/app`)** | ❌ **Khulta hi nahi** | Frontend login token bhejta hi nahi. Login screen bhi nahi hai, isliye API har request reject karti hai (401) |
| **AI se refund (LLM intake)** | ❌ **Kabhi poora nahi hota** | Bug: LLM key lagate hi har message "needs human review" ho jaata hai, kyunki confidence hamesha 0 rehta hai |
| **Google Gemini key** | ❌ Use hi nahi hoti | Code mein Gemini ka option hi nahi hai (sirf Anthropic aur OpenAI) |
| Onboarding | ⚠️ Adhoora | Login nahi hai, neatlogs key ka step nahi hai, Gemini nahi hai |
| Encryption key | ⚠️ Risk | Key missing ya badal gayi to poori API 500 error dene lagti hai |
| Git ledger (Entire evidence) | ⚠️ Galat jagah | Commits ek alag hidden repo (`data/ledger-repo`) mein jaate hain, main repo mein nahi. Isliye judges ko kuch nahi dikhega |
| neatlogs spans | ⚠️ Kamzor | Detections error ki tarah nahi dikhti, timing ka matlab nahi banta, aur yeh code abhi commit nahi hua |
| Hard-coding | ⚠️ Bahut | Har jagah "refund" likha hai, 5 sample orders fix hain, USD fix hai, aur cfo ke numbers sirf constants hain, asli runs se nahi aate |
| Dashboard UI | ⚠️ Feeka | Koi live dial nahi, koi chart nahi, neatlogs ka status nahi, aur demo flow guided nahi hai |

## Plan (Monday 7 PM IST submission ko dhyaan mein rakhkar)

**Phase 1: Jo toota hai woh theek karna (sabse zaroori)**
- **Access screen:** "Try the demo" pe ek click se local demo session milega (safe flag ke peeche). "Connect workspace" se token daalne ka option. Frontend har request ke saath token bhejega.
- **LLM intake bug fix:** confidence model se aayega, aur model ka jawab ```json``` fences mein ho tab bhi parse hoga.
- **Encryption key** missing hone pe saaf error message, crash nahi. Onboarding ki validation bhi save karne se pehle hogi.
- **neatlogs:** project naam bhejna, detections ko error status dena, spans ki asli timing, aur yeh sab commit karna.

**Phase 2: Providers aur onboarding**
- Providers: **Gemini** (neatlogs khud Gemini calls ko trace karta hai, bonus), Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible, aur bina key wala demo mode.
- Onboarding: Workspace → Model + key + **Test** → **neatlogs key + Test** → Rules → Data → Review. Saari keys encrypted save hongi aur screen pe masked dikhengi.

**Phase 3: Hard-coding hatana**
- **Task-class registry** config se: har class ka ceiling, kitne clean runs pe promote, aur currency. "Refund" ke saath ek doosri class, taaki demo mein dikhe ki ek class gir gayi aur doosri apne level pe rahi.
- Frontend saare labels, templates aur sample data API se lega.
- **cfo model asli runs ke numbers se** calculate hoga.

**Phase 4: Dashboard redesign, "Mission Control"**
- Har task class ka **live autonomy dial** (animated), saath mein streak jaise "7/10 clean"
- **Trust timeline chart:** level time ke saath kaise badla, detections ke markers ke saath
- **Before/after metrics:** kitne runs verify hue, kitni false success pakdi gayi, kitna supervision $ bacha
- **Status chips:** neatlogs connected, LLM provider, ledger
- **Inline approve**, aur thodi-thodi der mein auto-refresh

**Phase 5: Wow features (neeche se chuno)**

**Phase 6: Evidence aur submission**
- `EVIDENCE.md`, 50+50 runs ka report, Entire graph ka output, README aur video script ka update

"""The refund worker — the end-to-end task loop.

One run does exactly this, in order, tracing every step:

    1. read the license for the task class;
    2. decide what is *authorised* (pure license logic);
    3. plan around that decision;
    4. execute only what is authorised (a fault may push it beyond — on
       purpose, to be caught);
    5. verify the side effect by reading SQLite back — never trusting the tool;
    6. run the detections; any hit demotes, otherwise a clean executed run
       earns track-record credit;
    7. persist the run, its spans, its detections, and the dial change.

Authority lives in :func:`sololicense.domain.license.decide`; truth lives in
the verifier. The worker only wires them together.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from sololicense.agent.planner import Plan, Planner
from sololicense.agent.tools import execute_refund
from sololicense.config import Config
from sololicense.db.repositories import detections as detections_repo
from sololicense.db.repositories import runs as runs_repo
from sololicense.db.repositories.runs import NewRun, insert_run
from sololicense.domain.license import Decision, LicenseLevel, decide
from sololicense.domain.models import FaultMode, RefundRequest, RunStatus
from sololicense.faults.injector import FaultInjector, effects_for
from sololicense.observability import detections as rules
from sololicense.observability.detections import Detection
from sololicense.observability.tracer import Tracer
from sololicense.services import verification
from sololicense.security import Actor
from sololicense.services.license_service import LicenseService, SYSTEM_ACTOR, Transition

_EXECUTING = (Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE, Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunResult:
    """Everything the UI needs to render one completed run."""

    run_id: int
    task_class: str
    status: RunStatus
    authorized: Decision
    attempted: Decision
    before_refunded: float
    after_refunded: float
    trace_id: str
    plan: Plan
    transition: Transition
    detections: list[Detection] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def actual_delta(self) -> float:
        return round(self.after_refunded - self.before_refunded, 2)


class RefundWorker:
    def __init__(
        self,
        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
        config: Config,
        *,
        tracer: Tracer,
        license_service: LicenseService,
        fault_injector: FaultInjector,
        planner: Planner,
    ) -> None:
        self._conn = conn
        self._config = config
        self._tracer = tracer
        self._licenses = license_service
        self._faults = fault_injector
        self._planner = planner

    def run_refund(
        self,
        request: RefundRequest,
        *,
        task_class: str = "refund",
        approved: bool = False,
        idempotency_key: str | None = None,
        actor: Actor = SYSTEM_ACTOR,
    ) -> RunResult:
        trace = self._tracer.start_trace("refund")
        try:
            return self._run_refund(
                request,
                task_class=task_class,
                approved=approved,
                idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
                actor=actor,
                trace=trace,
            )
        except Exception as error:
            trace.span("run.error", status="error", error_type=type(error).__name__)
            trace.close()
            raise

    def _run_refund(
        self,
        request: RefundRequest,
        *,
        task_class: str,
        approved: bool,
        idempotency_key: str | None,
        actor: Actor,
        trace,
    ) -> RunResult:
        state = self._licenses.get_or_create(task_class)
        # Peek, don't consume: an armed fault only bends a run that actually
        # executes, so a draft or suggestion leaves it armed for the next one.
        armed_effects = effects_for(self._faults.peek(task_class))
        trace.span(
            "license.check",
            level=state.effective_level.name,
            quarantined=state.quarantined,
            fault=armed_effects.mode.value,
        )

        authorized = self._authorize(state, request, approved)
        attempted = self._attempt(authorized, state, armed_effects)
        plan = self._planner.plan(request, authorized, state)
        trace.span("plan", source=plan.source, rationale=plan.rationale)

        before = verification.read_refunded(self._conn, request.order_id)
        will_execute = attempted in _EXECUTING
        duplicate = (
            bool(idempotency_key)
            and will_execute
            and runs_repo.get_executed_by_idempotency_key(
                self._conn, idempotency_key or ""
            )
            is not None
        )
        if duplicate:
            will_execute = False
        effects = effects_for(FaultMode.NONE)
        if will_execute and armed_effects.active:
            effects = self._faults.consume_effects(task_class)
        intended_delta = request.amount if will_execute else 0.0

        if will_execute:
            self._do_execute(trace, request, effects)
        else:
            trace.span("execute.skipped", reason=attempted.name)

        if will_execute and effects.skip_verification:
            result = verification.missing_refund_verification(
                before=before,
                intended_delta=intended_delta,
            )
        else:
            result = verification.verify_refund(
                self._conn,
                order_id=request.order_id,
                before=before,
                intended_delta=intended_delta,
            )
        trace.span(
            "verify.readback",
            before=result.before,
            after=result.after,
            actual_delta=result.actual_delta,
            intended_delta=intended_delta,
            matched=result.matched,
            verified=result.verified,
        )

        found = self._run_detections(
            authorized=authorized,
            attempted=attempted,
            intended_delta=intended_delta,
            result=result,
            duplicate=duplicate,
        )
        for d in found:
            trace.span(f"detection.{d.rule}", status="error", severity=d.severity,
                       message=d.message)

        status = self._status(found, will_execute, authorized)
        run_id = self._persist_run(
            request=request,
            task_class=task_class,
            state_level=state.effective_level,
            authorized=authorized,
            status=status,
            executed=will_execute,
            result=result,
            idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
            actor=actor,
            effects=effects,
            trace=trace,
            plan=plan,
        )
        trace.flush(self._conn, run_id)

        for d in found:
            detections_repo.insert_detection(
                self._conn,
                run_id=run_id,
                rule=d.rule,
                severity=d.severity,
                message=d.message,
                trace_id=trace.trace_id,
            )

        transition = self._update_dial(
            task_class, status, found, run_id, trace.trace_id, actor
        )
        self._conn.commit()

        return RunResult(
            run_id=run_id,
            task_class=task_class,
            status=status,
            authorized=authorized,
            attempted=attempted,
            before_refunded=result.before,
            after_refunded=result.after,
            trace_id=trace.trace_id,
            plan=plan,
            transition=transition,
            detections=found,
        )

    # --- helpers ---------------------------------------------------------

    def _authorize(
        self, state, request: RefundRequest, approved: bool
    ) -> Decision:
        """What the license authorises. A human approval grants execution at
        the level's audit posture (L3 keeps the audited variant)."""
        if approved and not state.quarantined:
            return (
                Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED
                if state.level is LicenseLevel.L3
                else Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE
            )
        return decide(
            state, request.amount, l2_ceiling=self._config.l2_auto_refund_ceiling
        )

    def _attempt(self, authorized: Decision, state, effects) -> Decision:
        """What the agent actually attempts. The policy-violation fault pushes
        it to auto-execute even when that is not authorised."""
        if effects.force_auto_execute:
            return (
                Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED
                if state.level is LicenseLevel.L3
                else Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE
            )
        return authorized

    def _do_execute(self, trace, request: RefundRequest, effects) -> None:
        trace.span(
            "tool.execute_refund",
            order_id=request.order_id,
            amount=request.amount,
            suppress_write=effects.suppress_write,
        )
        tool_result = execute_refund(
            self._conn,
            order_id=request.order_id,
            amount=request.amount,
            suppress_write=effects.suppress_write,
        )
        # The tool's claim is recorded but explicitly marked untrusted.
        trace.span(
            "tool.result", ok=tool_result.ok, message=tool_result.message,
            trusted=False,
        )

    def _run_detections(
        self, *, authorized, attempted, intended_delta, result, duplicate
    ) -> list[Detection]:
        candidates = [
            rules.detect_policy_breach(authorized=authorized, attempted=attempted),
            rules.detect_duplicate_action(duplicate=duplicate),
            rules.detect_state_mismatch(
                intended_delta=intended_delta,
                actual_delta=result.actual_delta,
                verified=result.verified,
            ),
            rules.detect_missing_verification(verified=result.verified),
        ]
        return [d for d in candidates if d is not None]

    def _status(self, found, will_execute, authorized) -> RunStatus:
        if found:
            return RunStatus.DEMOTED
        if will_execute:
            return RunStatus.CLEAN
        if authorized is Decision.DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL:
            return RunStatus.PENDING_APPROVAL
        return RunStatus.SUGGESTED

    def _persist_run(
        self, *, request, task_class, state_level, authorized, status, executed,
        result, idempotency_key, actor, effects, trace, plan,
    ) -> int:
        return insert_run(
            self._conn,
            NewRun(
                task_class=task_class,
                order_id=request.order_id,
                requested_amount=request.amount,
                level_at_run=int(state_level),
                decision=authorized.name,
                status=status.value,
                executed=executed and status is not RunStatus.SUGGESTED,
                before_refunded=result.before,
                after_refunded=result.after,
                idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
                actor_id=actor.actor_id,
                actor_role=actor.role.value,
                fault_mode=effects.mode.value,
                trace_id=trace.trace_id,
                notes=plan.rationale,
            ),
        )

    def _update_dial(
        self, task_class, status, found, run_id, trace_id, actor
    ) -> Transition:
        if status is RunStatus.DEMOTED:
            reason = "; ".join(d.message for d in found)
            return self._licenses.apply_detection(
                task_class, run_id=run_id, trace_id=trace_id, reason=reason, actor=actor
            )
        if status is RunStatus.CLEAN:
            return self._licenses.apply_clean_run(
                task_class, run_id=run_id, trace_id=trace_id, actor=actor
            )
        # Suggestions and pending approvals do not move the dial.
        state = self._licenses.get_or_create(task_class)
        return Transition(old=state, new=state, kind="noop", git_sha=None)
"""Tools the refund worker can call.

Deliberately, ``execute_refund`` reports success even when a fault suppressed
the write. That models the real hazard the whole project is about: a tool's
response is not proof of a side effect. Only :mod:`sololicense.services.
verification` — which reads SQLite back — is trusted."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass

from sololicense.db.repositories import orders as orders_repo


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ToolResult:
    """What a tool claims happened. Treated as a claim, never as evidence."""

    ok: bool
    message: str


def execute_refund(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
    *,
    order_id: str,
    amount: float,
    suppress_write: bool,
) -> ToolResult:
    """Attempt to refund ``amount`` against ``order_id``.

    When ``suppress_write`` is set (quiet-failure fault) the database is left
    untouched but the tool still returns ``ok=True`` — exactly the lie the
    verifier is there to catch. The caller commits on a real write.
    """
    if suppress_write:
        return ToolResult(ok=True, message="Refund processed (reported).")

    orders_repo.apply_refund(conn, order_id, amount)
    return ToolResult(ok=True, message="Refund processed.")
"""Value objects that travel through the refund loop.

These are plain, immutable carriers of data — no behaviour, no I/O. They give
the rest of the system a shared vocabulary (a ``RefundRequest`` means the same
thing to the agent, the verifier, and the UI)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum


class RunStatus(str, Enum):
    """Terminal status of a single refund run, from the agent's point of view."""

    SUGGESTED = "suggested"            # L0 / quarantined: advice only
    PENDING_APPROVAL = "pending_approval"  # L1 or over-ceiling: awaits a human
    CLEAN = "clean"                    # executed and verified against SQLite
    DEMOTED = "demoted"                # a detection fired; license crashed
    APPROVED = "approved"              # superseded by a human-approved run


class FaultMode(str, Enum):
    """Deterministic faults the injector can arm for the next run."""

    NONE = "none"
    QUIET_FAILURE = "quiet_failure"      # tool reports success, DB unchanged
    POLICY_VIOLATION = "policy_violation"  # action exceeds the current license
    SKIP_VERIFICATION = "skip_verification"  # execute, then skip read-back


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RefundRequest:
    """A customer refund to be worked by the agent."""

    order_id: str
    customer: str
    amount: float
    reason: str

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.amount < 0:
            raise ValueError("refund amount cannot be negative")
        if not self.order_id:
            raise ValueError("order_id is required")
"""Composition root.

The one place where concrete dependencies are constructed and wired. Both the
Streamlit UI and the command-line scripts build their world through
:func:`build_app`, so there is a single, consistent assembly order — and
neatlogs is initialised here, before any agent object exists, as required."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass

from sololicense.agent.planner import Planner
from sololicense.agent.worker import RefundWorker
from sololicense.config import Config, load_config, with_overrides
from sololicense.db.repositories import settings as settings_repo
from sololicense.db.database import init_db
from sololicense.faults.injector import FaultInjector
from sololicense.observability.neatlogs_client import NeatlogsClient, init_neatlogs
from sololicense.observability.tracer import Tracer
from sololicense.services.git_ledger import GitLedger
from sololicense.services.license_service import LicenseService


@dataclass
class AppContext:
    """Fully wired application, ready to serve a UI or a script."""

    config: Config
    conn: sqlite3.Connection
    neatlogs: NeatlogsClient
    worker: RefundWorker
    license_service: LicenseService
    fault_injector: FaultInjector


def build_app(
    config: Config | None = None, *, check_same_thread: bool = True
) -> AppContext:
    config = config or load_config()

    # 1. Persistence first, so operator settings can override the environment.
    conn = init_db(config.db_path, check_same_thread=check_same_thread)
    stored_settings = settings_repo.get_all(conn)
    config = with_overrides(
        config,
        settings_repo.reveal_secret_values(stored_settings, config.settings_encryption_key),
    )

    # 2. Observability — instrument before any agent logic.
    neatlogs = init_neatlogs(config)
    tracer = Tracer(neatlogs)

    # 3. Services and the agent.
    license_service = LicenseService(
        conn, GitLedger(repo_root=config.ledger_repo),
        promotion_threshold=config.promotion_clean_runs,
    )
    fault_injector = FaultInjector(conn)
    planner = Planner(config)
    worker = RefundWorker(
        conn,
        config,
        tracer=tracer,
        license_service=license_service,
        fault_injector=fault_injector,
        planner=planner,
    )

    return AppContext(
        config=config,
        conn=conn,
        neatlogs=neatlogs,
        worker=worker,
        license_service=license_service,
        fault_injector=fault_injector,
    )

"""The autonomy ladder and its state machine.

A *task class* (e.g. ``refund``) holds one :class:`LicenseState`. The agent may
only do what the current level permits. Levels are *earned* by consecutive
clean runs and *lost* immediately when a detection fires.

    L0  suggest only                       (human does everything)
    L1  draft + human approves each run
    L2  auto-execute under a dollar ceiling
    L3  full auto, post-hoc audit

Design notes
------------
* This module is pure: given the same inputs it always returns the same
  outputs and never touches a database, clock, or network. Persistence and
  side effects live in outer layers.
* A detection demotes the class straight to ``L0`` *and* quarantines it.
  While quarantined the class behaves at L0 and **cannot** auto-promote —
  only a human-reviewed evidence packet (``restore``) clears the quarantine.
  This is what makes recovery "with judgment, not blind retry".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from enum import IntEnum


class LicenseLevel(IntEnum):
    """Rungs on the autonomy ladder. Ordered, so comparisons are meaningful."""

    L0 = 0  # suggest only
    L1 = 1  # draft + human approve
    L2 = 2  # auto under a threshold
    L3 = 3  # full auto with post-hoc audit

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        return {
            LicenseLevel.L0: "Suggest only",
            LicenseLevel.L1: "Draft + approve",
            LicenseLevel.L2: "Auto under ceiling",
            LicenseLevel.L3: "Full auto (audited)",
        }[self]


class Decision(IntEnum):
    """What the agent is permitted to do with a specific refund request."""

    SUGGEST = 0            # produce a recommendation only; no execution
    DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL = 1  # prepare the change; a human must approve it
    AUTO_EXECUTE = 2        # execute now within policy
    AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED = 3  # execute now, flagged for post-hoc audit


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LicenseState:
    """Immutable snapshot of one task class's standing on the ladder.

    Instances are never mutated in place; every transition returns a new
    state, which keeps the state machine easy to reason about and test.
    """

    task_class: str
    level: LicenseLevel = LicenseLevel.L0
    consecutive_clean_runs: int = 0
    quarantined: bool = False
    # Level the class held before the most recent detection demotion, so a
    # reviewer can see "it fell from L2" when deciding how far to restore.
    demoted_from: LicenseLevel | None = None

    @property
    def effective_level(self) -> LicenseLevel:
        """Level actually in force. A quarantined class always acts at L0."""
        return LicenseLevel.L0 if self.quarantined else self.level


def decide(
    state: LicenseState,
    amount: float,
    *,
    l2_ceiling: float,
) -> Decision:
    """Resolve what the agent may do for a refund of ``amount`` dollars.

    This is the single authority on permissions. The worker must route every
    request through it and must never execute a side effect the returned
    :class:`Decision` does not authorise.
    """
    if amount < 0:
        raise ValueError("refund amount cannot be negative")

    level = state.effective_level

    if level is LicenseLevel.L0:
        return Decision.SUGGEST
    if level is LicenseLevel.L1:
        return Decision.DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL
    if level is LicenseLevel.L2:
        # Auto only under the ceiling; anything above falls back to approval.
        if amount <= l2_ceiling:
            return Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE
        return Decision.DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL
    return Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED  # L3


def record_clean_run(
    state: LicenseState,
    *,
    promotion_threshold: int,
) -> LicenseState:
    """Advance the track record after a verified-clean run.

    A quarantined class accrues no credit — it must be restored by a human
    first. Reaching ``promotion_threshold`` consecutive clean runs promotes
    the class one rung and resets the counter.
    """
    if state.quarantined:
        return state

    tally = state.consecutive_clean_runs + 1

    if state.level < LicenseLevel.L3 and tally >= promotion_threshold:
        return replace(
            state,
            level=LicenseLevel(state.level + 1),
            consecutive_clean_runs=0,
            demoted_from=None,
        )

    return replace(state, consecutive_clean_runs=tally, demoted_from=None)


def demote_on_detection(state: LicenseState) -> LicenseState:
    """Crash the class to L0 and quarantine it. Called the instant a
    detection fires. Idempotent in spirit: re-detecting a quarantined class
    keeps it quarantined and remembers the highest level it fell from."""
    fell_from = state.demoted_from if state.quarantined else state.level
    return replace(
        state,
        level=LicenseLevel.L0,
        consecutive_clean_runs=0,
        quarantined=True,
        demoted_from=fell_from,
    )


def restore(state: LicenseState, target: LicenseLevel) -> LicenseState:
    """Lift the quarantine and set the class to a human-chosen level.

    Only ever called after a reviewer has read the evidence packet, so the
    judgement lives with the human; this function just applies the decision.
    """
    return replace(
        state,
        level=target,
        consecutive_clean_runs=0,
        quarantined=False,
        demoted_from=None,
    )
"""License service — the one orchestrator allowed to change the dial.

It composes the pure state machine (:mod:`sololicense.domain.license`) with
persistence, the event ledger, and the git ledger. Every transition it makes
is: compute new state → persist state + event (SQLite) → commit a git ledger
entry → back-link the git sha to the event.

Only three things move the dial, and they map one-to-one onto the ladder's
rules:
    * a verified-clean run may *promote*;
    * a detection *demotes* (crash to L0 + quarantine);
    * a human *restores* after reading the evidence packet.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass

from sololicense.db.repositories import events as events_repo
from sololicense.db.repositories import license as license_repo
from sololicense.domain.license import (
    LicenseLevel,
    LicenseState,
    demote_on_detection,
    record_clean_run,
    restore,
)
from sololicense.services.git_ledger import GitLedger, LedgerEntry
from sololicense.security import Actor, Role


SYSTEM_ACTOR = Actor("system:license-service", Role.ADMIN)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Transition:
    """Result of a dial change, surfaced to the worker and UI."""

    old: LicenseState
    new: LicenseState
    kind: str            # promote | demote | restore | noop
    git_sha: str | None


class LicenseService:
    def __init__(
        self,
        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
        ledger: GitLedger,
        *,
        promotion_threshold: int,
    ) -> None:
        self._conn = conn
        self._ledger = ledger
        self._threshold = promotion_threshold

    def get_or_create(self, task_class: str) -> LicenseState:
        """Return the task class's state, seeding a fresh L0 row if absent."""
        state = license_repo.get_state(self._conn, task_class)
        if state is None:
            state = LicenseState(task_class=task_class)
            license_repo.upsert_state(self._conn, state)
            self._conn.commit()
        return state

    def apply_clean_run(
        self,
        task_class: str,
        *,
        run_id: int | None,
        trace_id: str | None,
        actor: Actor = SYSTEM_ACTOR,
    ) -> Transition:
        """Credit a verified-clean run; promote if the threshold is reached."""
        old = self.get_or_create(task_class)
        new = record_clean_run(old, promotion_threshold=self._threshold)
        if new.level > old.level:
            return self._persist(
                old,
                new,
                kind="promote",
                reason=(
                    f"{self._threshold} consecutive clean runs; earned "
                    f"{new.level.name} ({new.level.label})."
                ),
                run_id=run_id,
                trace_id=trace_id,
                actor=actor,
            )
        # No rung change: persist the updated tally without a git event.
        license_repo.upsert_state(self._conn, new)
        self._conn.commit()
        return Transition(old=old, new=new, kind="noop", git_sha=None)

    def apply_detection(
        self,
        task_class: str,
        *,
        run_id: int | None,
        trace_id: str | None,
        reason: str,
        actor: Actor = SYSTEM_ACTOR,
    ) -> Transition:
        """Crash the dial to L0 and quarantine on a detection."""
        old = self.get_or_create(task_class)
        new = demote_on_detection(old)
        return self._persist(
            old,
            new,
            kind="demote",
            reason=reason,
            run_id=run_id,
            trace_id=trace_id,
            actor=actor,
        )

    def restore_license(
        self,
        task_class: str,
        target: LicenseLevel,
        *,
        reason: str,
        actor: Actor = SYSTEM_ACTOR,
    ) -> Transition:
        """Lift quarantine to a human-chosen level after evidence review."""
        old = self.get_or_create(task_class)
        new = restore(old, target)
        return self._persist(
            old,
            new,
            kind="restore",
            reason=reason,
            run_id=None,
            trace_id=None,
            actor=actor,
        )

    def _persist(
        self,
        old: LicenseState,
        new: LicenseState,
        *,
        kind: str,
        reason: str,
        run_id: int | None,
        trace_id: str | None,
        actor: Actor,
    ) -> Transition:
        """Persist state + event, then commit a git ledger entry and link it."""
        license_repo.upsert_state(self._conn, new)
        event_id = events_repo.insert_event(
            self._conn,
            task_class=new.task_class,
            kind=kind,
            from_level=int(old.level),
            to_level=int(new.level),
            reason=reason,
            run_id=run_id,
            actor_id=actor.actor_id,
            actor_role=actor.role.value,
        )
        self._conn.commit()

        git_sha = self._ledger.record(
            LedgerEntry(
                task_class=new.task_class,
                kind=kind,
                from_level=int(old.level),
                to_level=int(new.level),
                reason=reason,
                run_id=run_id,
                trace_id=trace_id,
            )
        )
        if git_sha:
            events_repo.set_git_sha(self._conn, event_id, git_sha)
            self._conn.commit()

        return Transition(old=old, new=new, kind=kind, git_sha=git_sha)
"""Git-backed license ledger.

Every autonomy change (promote / demote / restore) appends one line to
``ledger/license_ledger.jsonl`` and commits *only that file*. The commit is the
Entire-compatible checkpoint: its history is the graph of how a task class
earned and lost its license, and each message explains the change.

Commits are scoped to the ledger file so running the app never sweeps up
unrelated working-tree edits. If git is unavailable the ledger line is still
written and the caller simply gets ``None`` for the sha — the app keeps working.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
_LEDGER_RELPATH = Path("ledger") / "license_ledger.jsonl"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LedgerEntry:
    task_class: str
    kind: str          # promote | demote | restore
    from_level: int
    to_level: int
    reason: str
    run_id: int | None
    trace_id: str | None


def _commit_message(entry: LedgerEntry) -> str:
    """Human- and Entire-readable message describing one license change."""
    verb = {
        "promote": "promote",
        "demote": "demote",
        "restore": "restore",
    }.get(entry.kind, entry.kind)
    title = (
        f"license({entry.task_class}): {verb} L{entry.from_level}"
        f" -> L{entry.to_level}"
    )
    body = [title, "", entry.reason]
    if entry.run_id is not None:
        body.append(f"run: {entry.run_id}")
    if entry.trace_id:
        body.append(f"trace: {entry.trace_id}")
    return "\n".join(body)


class GitLedger:
    """Appends to and commits the license ledger file.

    ``repo_root`` defaults to this repository; tests point it at a throwaway
    git repo so committing is exercised without touching project history."""

    def __init__(self, repo_root: Path = _REPO_ROOT) -> None:
        self._repo_root = repo_root
        self._ledger_file = repo_root / _LEDGER_RELPATH

    def record(self, entry: LedgerEntry) -> str | None:
        """Append the entry and commit the ledger file. Returns the short sha,
        or ``None`` if git is unavailable or nothing needed committing."""
        self._append(entry)
        return self._commit(entry)

    def _run_git(self, args: list[str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        return subprocess.run(
            ["git", *args],
            cwd=self._repo_root,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
        )

    def _ensure_repo(self) -> None:
        self._repo_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if not (self._repo_root / ".git").exists():
            self._run_git(["init", "-q"])
        self._run_git(["config", "user.name", "Solo License"])
        self._run_git(["config", "user.email", "solo-license@example.invalid"])

    def _append(self, entry: LedgerEntry) -> None:
        self._ledger_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        line = json.dumps(
            {
                "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                "task_class": entry.task_class,
                "kind": entry.kind,
                "from_level": entry.from_level,
                "to_level": entry.to_level,
                "reason": entry.reason,
                "run_id": entry.run_id,
                "trace_id": entry.trace_id,
            }
        )
        with self._ledger_file.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(line + "\n")

    def _commit(self, entry: LedgerEntry) -> str | None:
        self._ensure_repo()
        rel = _LEDGER_RELPATH.as_posix()
        add = self._run_git(["add", "--", rel])
        if add.returncode != 0:
            return None
        commit = self._run_git(["commit", "-m", _commit_message(entry), "--", rel])
        if commit.returncode != 0:
            return None
        sha = self._run_git(["rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"])
        return sha.stdout.strip() or None

PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;

-- The "real world" the agent acts on. orders.refunded_amount is the ONLY
-- authority on whether a refund actually landed — the verifier reads it
-- back after every execution rather than trusting the tool's response.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS orders (
    order_id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer         TEXT NOT NULL,
    amount           REAL NOT NULL,            -- original order total
    refunded_amount  REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- verified side effect
    status           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'paid',
